name: Should I choose a single-level or two-tier kitchen island?

mainEntity.name: Should I choose a single-level or two-tier kitchen island?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard kitchen island is built at counter height, which is 36 inches from the floor, ideal for food prep and casual seating using 24-inch counter stools. A two-tier island adds a 42-inch raised bar top. The raised tier hides countertop clutter from adjacent living areas and separates cooking zones from dining guests. However, single-level islands provide one continuous, uninterrupted surface that is more versatile for baking, serving buffets, and accommodating open-concept entertaining. Your entertaining habits and kitchen visibility determine which design fits best.
acceptedAnswer.description: Single-level 36-inch islands maximize continuous prep surface, while two-tier 42-inch islands conceal dirty dishes and separate dining guests from cooking areas.
